title: Now Christ the God to Earth Hath Come
description: Now Christ the God to Earth Hath Come in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now Christ the God to earth hath come, And made our dwell-ing place His home; And in our flesh the God Man gives The life by which His peo-ple lives.

lines: Now Christ the God to earth hath come,
And made our dwelling place His home;
And in our flesh the God-Man gives
The life by which His people lives.
Bound to the Cross He bleeding dies,
That man from sin forgiven may rise;
And by the grace of God set free,
Live in His service endlessly.
They who in Adam sinning fell,
With Christ ascend with God to dwell;
And through the pain the Saviour bore,
Are freed from pain for evermore.
And where the Christ 'mong myriads bright
Sits on His throne of peerless light,
There dwell the saints who by His grace
Share on the throne the victor's place.
Glory to Thee, our Father, God,
Who dwell'st in heaven, Thy high abode;
Glory to Thee, O Christ the Son,
And Holy Ghost, blest Three in One.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
